task.schedulingTaskCreated.name: com.qlik.scheduling.task.created
task.schedulingTaskCreated.title: Task created

eventType.description: Unique identifier for the event type.

task.schedulingTaskCreated.description: Published when a new task is created. The event includes the task ID, owner, associated resource, and the scheduled action.

task.schedulingTaskDeleted.name: com.qlik.scheduling.task.deleted
task.schedulingTaskDeleted.title: Task deleted

eventType.description: Unique identifier for the event type.

task.schedulingTaskDeleted.description: Published when a task is deleted. The event includes the full task state at the time of deletion, including the task ID and owner.

task.schedulingTaskUpdated.name: com.qlik.scheduling.task.updated
task.schedulingTaskUpdated.title: Task updated

path.description: The JSON path of the field that was updated.

newValue.description: The new value of the field after the update.

oldValue.description: The previous value of the field before the update.

items.description: An object describing a single field that was updated.

_updates.description: The list of fields updated in this task, with the old and new values for each changed field.

eventType.description: Unique identifier for the event type.

task.schedulingTaskUpdated.description: Published when a task's configuration or properties are updated. The event includes the updated task state along with a list of changed fields in `_updates`, identifying what was modified and the old and new values. Use this to detect configuration drift or audit changes to scheduled tasks.

time.description: Timestamp of when the occurrence happened. Must adhere to RFC 3339.

type.description: Describes the type of event related to the originating occurrence.

source.description: Identifies the context in which an event happened.

specversion.description: The version of the CloudEvents specification which the event uses.

datacontenttype.description: Content type of the data value. Must adhere to RFC 2046 format.

userid.description: Unique identifier of the user related to the event.

tenantid.description: Unique identifier of the tenant related to the event.

toplevelresourceid.description: Identifier of the top-level resource that triggered the event.

id.description: The unique identifier of the task.

usage.description: The product domain in which the associated resource is used, such as `ANALYTICS` or `DATA_PREPARATION`. Defaults to `ANALYTICS` when not specified.

action.description: The action performed on the target resource.

status.description: The status in which the task run finished. One of `succeeded`, `failed`, or `aborted`.

enabled.description: Whether the task is enabled. When `true`, the task is active and eligible to run.

ownerId.description: The unique identifier of the user that owns the task. Only applicable for user-level tasks.

spaceId.description: The unique identifier of the space the task operates in.

duration.description: The task execution duration in ISO 8601 format.

createdAt.description: The UTC timestamp when the task was created.

createdBy.description: The unique identifier of the user that created the task.

deletedAt.description: The UTC timestamp when the task was deleted.

updatedAt.description: The UTC timestamp when the task was last updated.

resourceId.description: The unique identifier of the target resource associated with the task's action.

description.description: A user-provided description of the task.

actionParams.description: The list of parameters for the action.

disabledCode.description: The reason the task was disabled.

migratedFrom.description: The identifier of the original reload task from which this task was migrated. Empty if the task was not migrated.

resourceType.description: The type of resource the task operates on.

statusDetails.description: Additional details about the final status, such as the failure reason, automation ID, or reload ID.

taskEntryObject.description: Represents the full state of a task resource at the time the event was published. All lifecycle events carry this object as their `data` payload, capturing the task's configuration, ownership, and execution status.
